RM_ee8c853f-75c4-4771-9e07-c945b8a9f349.cn: <Noises> 或者你够大胆的话, 甚至可以用研钵和杵…<Noises>

RM_ef323d59-b334-4635-9969-d0a404c1d578.ch: 今天我們要沖泡的是… 咖啡
RM_ef323d59-b334-4635-9969-d0a404c1d578.cn: 今天我们要冲泡的是… 咖啡

RM_ETC_FA1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sound of metal clanging echoes faintly in the background.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **背景隱約迴盪著金屬敲擊的聲響.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **背景隐约回荡着金属敲击的声响.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_FA1_Line02.en: Welcome to 'Forge Ahead,' your guide to survival crafting.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line02.ch: 歡迎收看《鍛造前行》, 你的求生製作指南.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line02.cn: 欢迎收看《锻造前行》, 你的求生制作指南.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line03.en: I'm Rick, a former army engineer, here to help you turn scraps into survival tools.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line03.ch: 我是瑞克, 以前是陸軍工兵, 今天要教各位把廢料變成求生工具.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line03.cn: 我是瑞克, 以前是陆军工兵, 今天要教各位把废料变成求生工具.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line04.en: Today, we'll learn how to make a basic barricade using salvaged sheet metal.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來學怎麼用撿回來的金屬板做一道簡易路障.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line04.cn: 今天我们要来学怎么用捡回来的金属板做一道简易路障.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line05.en: First, look for old appliances or wrecked vehicles they're treasure troves.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line05.ch: 首先, 去找老舊家電或報廢車輛, 那些都是寶庫.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line05.cn: 首先, 去找老旧家电或报废车辆, 那些都是宝库.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line06.en: To shape the metal, you'll need a hammer or a sturdy rock.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line06.ch: 要把金屬敲成形, 你需要一把鎚子, 或是一塊夠硬的石頭.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line06.cn: 要把金属敲成形, 你需要一把锤子, 或是一块够硬的石头.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line07.en: Yeah, it's crude, but it works. Bend it over something solid, like a cinder block.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line07.ch: 沒錯, 手法是很粗糙, 但管用. 找個硬東西把它折彎, 像水泥磚就行.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line07.cn: 没错, 手法是很粗糙, 但管用. 找个硬东西把它折弯, 像水泥砖就行.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line08.en: Remember, sharp edges can cut deep, so wear gloves or wrap your hands in cloth if that's all you've got.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line08.ch: 記住, 金屬的銳邊割得很深, 所以一定要戴手套. 手邊只有布的話, 就拿布把手包起來.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line08.cn: 记住, 金属的锐边割得很深, 所以一定要戴手套. 手边只有布的话, 就拿布把手包起来.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line09.en: Metal is your friend out there.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line09.ch: 在外頭, 金屬是你的好夥伴.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line09.cn: 在外头, 金属是你的好伙伴.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line10.en: Strong, durable, and it doesn't rot.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line10.ch: 堅固, 耐用, 而且不會腐爛.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line10.cn: 坚固, 耐用, 而且不会腐烂.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line11.en: Stick with me, and you'll turn junk into defences that last.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line11.ch: 跟著我學, 你就能把廢鐵變成撐得住的防禦工事.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line11.cn: 跟着我学, 你就能把废铁变成撑得住的防御工事.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line12.en: Stay safe, folks. Remember, survival isn't pretty, but it works.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line12.ch: 各位, 注意安全. 記住, 求生不好看, 但活得下去.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line12.cn: 各位, 注意安全. 记住, 求生不好看, 但活得下去.

RM_ETC_FA1_Line13.en: I'll see you next time on 'Metal Matters.'
RM_ETC_FA1_Line13.ch: 我們《金屬大小事》下次見.
RM_ETC_FA1_Line13.cn: 我们《金属大小事》下次见.

RM_ETC_FA1_Title.ch: 鍛造前行: 求生製作
RM_ETC_FA1_Title.cn: 锻造前行: 求生制作

RM_ETC_FA2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sharp hiss of a welding torch fills the air.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **空氣中充滿焊槍尖銳的嘶嘶聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **空气中充满焊枪尖锐的嘶嘶声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_FA2_Line02.en: Hey folks, I'm Dave, and this is 'Forge Ahead.'
RM_ETC_FA2_Line02.ch: 嘿, 各位, 我是戴夫, 這裡是《鍛造前行》.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line02.cn: 嘿, 各位, 我是戴夫, 这里是《锻造前行》.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line03.en: Let's learn to weld like your life depends on it because it does.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line03.ch: 焊接這門功夫, 要當成小命全靠它一樣認真學, 因為事實本來就是這樣.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line03.cn: 焊接这门功夫, 要当成小命全靠它一样认真学, 因为事实本来就是这样.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line04.en: First tip: safety. No goggles? Use a tinted visor or sunglasses.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line04.ch: 第一個要訣: 安全. 沒有護目鏡? 拿有色面罩或太陽眼鏡頂著.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line04.cn: 第一个要诀: 安全. 没有护目镜? 拿有色面罩或墨镜顶着.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line05.en: Protect your eyes at all costs.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line05.ch: 無論如何都要保護好眼睛.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line05.cn: 无论如何都要保护好眼睛.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line06.en: Welding rods? Grab some from old tools or scrap metal.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line06.ch: 焊條呢? 從舊工具或廢金屬上弄一些就有了.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line06.cn: 焊条呢? 从旧工具或废金属上弄一些就有了.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line07.en: Start with small projects, like patching holes in a door or fence.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line07.ch: 先從小東西練起, 像是補門板或圍欄上的破洞.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line07.cn: 先从小东西练起, 像是补门板或围栏上的破洞.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line08.en: Keep your hands steady and take your time.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line09.en: A good weld can mean the difference between safety and a breach.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line09.ch: 焊得好不好, 差別就在守得住還是被攻破.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line09.cn: 焊得好不好, 差别就在守得住还是被攻破.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line10.en: Stay safe out there, and keep building.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line10.ch: 在外頭注意安全, 繼續動手做.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line10.cn: 在外头注意安全, 继续动手做.

RM_ETC_FA2_Line11.en: This is Dave, signing off from 'Forge Ahead.'
RM_ETC_FA2_Line11.ch: 我是戴夫, 《鍛造前行》下次再會.
RM_ETC_FA2_Line11.cn: 我是戴夫, 《锻造前行》下次再会.

RM_ETC_FA2_Title.en: Forge Ahead: Welding for Emergency Repairs
RM_ETC_FA2_Title.ch: 鍛造前行: 緊急修補焊接術
RM_ETC_FA2_Title.cn: 锻造前行: 紧急修补焊接术

RM_ETC_FA3_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sharp sizzle of a welding torch igniting is heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA3_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來焊槍點燃時尖銳的嘶嘶聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA3_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来焊枪点燃时尖锐的嘶嘶声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_FA3_Line02.en: Hello, I'm Dave, and this is 'Forge Ahead.'
RM_ETC_FA3_Line02.ch: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 這裡是《鍛造前行》.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line02.cn: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 这里是《锻造前行》.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line03.en: Today, we'll focus on repairing metal fences to secure your perimeter.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line03.ch: 今天我們要專講金屬圍欄的修補, 把你的外圍守好.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line03.cn: 今天我们要专讲金属围栏的修补, 把你的外围守好.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line04.en: Inspect the fence for rust or damage.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line04.ch: 先檢查圍欄有沒有生鏽或破損.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line04.cn: 先检查围栏有没有生锈或破损.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line05.en: Clean the area thoroughly before welding to ensure a strong bond.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line05.ch: 焊之前把要接的部位徹底清乾淨, 接合才會夠牢.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line05.cn: 焊之前把要接的部位彻底清干净, 接合才会够牢.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line06.en: Use available materials like metal scraps to reinforce weak spots.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line06.ch: 手邊有什麼就用什麼, 像廢金屬就能拿來補強脆弱的地方.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line06.cn: 手边有什么就用什么, 像废金属就能拿来加固脆弱的地方.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line07.en: A well-maintained fence can deter unwanted intrusions.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line07.ch: 保養得好的圍欄, 能擋掉不速之客.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line07.cn: 保养得好的围栏, 能挡掉不速之客.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line08.en: Safety is paramount. Always protect your eyes and hands when working with metal.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line08.ch: 安全第一. 處理金屬時, 永遠要保護好你的眼睛和雙手.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line08.cn: 安全第一. 处理金属时, 永远要保护好你的眼睛和双手.

RM_ETC_FA3_Line09.en: Stay vigilant, and keep forging ahead.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line09.ch: 保持警覺, 繼續鍛造前行.
RM_ETC_FA3_Line09.cn: 保持警惕, 继续锻造前行.

RM_ETC_FA3_Title.ch: 鍛造前行: 金屬圍欄修補
RM_ETC_FA3_Title.cn: 锻造前行: 金属围栏修补

RM_ETC_FA4_Line01.en: [img=music] **The gentle whoosh of a torch melting glass is heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA4_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來噴槍熔化玻璃時輕柔的呼呼聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA4_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来喷枪熔化玻璃时轻柔的呼呼声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_FA4_Line02.en: Welcome to 'Forge Ahead.' I'm Alice, here to explore glassworking!
RM_ETC_FA4_Line02.ch: 歡迎收看《鍛造前行》. 我是愛麗絲, 今天要帶大家認識玻璃工藝!
RM_ETC_FA4_Line02.cn: 欢迎收看《锻造前行》. 我是爱丽丝, 今天要带大家认识玻璃工艺!

RM_ETC_FA4_Line03.en: Broken windows can be a security risk.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line03.ch: 破掉的窗戶是個安全漏洞.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line03.cn: 损坏的窗户是个安全漏洞.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line04.en: Salvage glass panes from abandoned buildings to replace damaged ones.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line04.ch: 去廢棄建築裡拆玻璃, 拿來替換破掉的那幾片.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line04.cn: 去废弃建筑里拆玻璃, 拿来替换损坏的那几片.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line05.en: To cut glass, score it with a glass cutter or a sharp tool, then snap it along the line.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line05.ch: 要裁玻璃, 先用玻璃刀或尖銳工具劃出刻痕, 再沿著線把它折斷.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line05.cn: 要裁玻璃, 先用玻璃刀或尖锐工具划出刻痕, 再沿着线把它折断.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line06.en: Always wear gloves to protect your hands.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line06.ch: 記得全程戴手套保護雙手.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line06.cn: 记得全程戴手套保护双手.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line07.en: In emergencies, melted glass can be fashioned into simple containers or lenses.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line07.ch: 緊急的時候, 熔化的玻璃還能做成簡單的容器或鏡片.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line07.cn: 紧急的时候, 熔化的玻璃还能做成简单的容器或镜片.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line08.en: Heat it until pliable, then shape as needed.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line08.ch: 加熱到可以塑形, 再照你要的樣子捏出來.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line08.cn: 加热到可以塑形, 再照你要的样子捏出来.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line09.ch: 玻璃工藝需要耐心, 也需要小心.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line09.cn: 玻璃工艺需要耐心, 也需要小心.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line10.en: Practice these techniques to maintain your shelter and tools.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line10.ch: 多練這幾招, 就能把你的住處和工具維護好.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line10.cn: 多练这几招, 就能把你的住处和工具维护好.

RM_ETC_FA4_Line11.en: Stay safe, and join me next time on 'Forge Ahead.'
RM_ETC_FA4_Line11.ch: 注意安全, 下次《鍛造前行》再見.
RM_ETC_FA4_Line11.cn: 注意安全, 下次《锻造前行》再见.

RM_ETC_FA4_Title.ch: 鍛造前行: 玻璃工藝
RM_ETC_FA4_Title.cn: 锻造前行: 玻璃工艺

RM_ETC_FA5_Line01.en: [img=music] **The rhythmic sound of trowel against brick is faintly audible.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA5_Line01.ch: [img=music] **隱約可以聽見抹刀敲在磚上的規律聲響.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_FA5_Line01.cn: [img=music] **隐约可以听见抹刀敲在砖上的规律声响.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_FA5_Line02.en: Hello, I'm Dave, and this is 'Forge Ahead.'
RM_ETC_FA5_Line02.ch: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 這裡是《鍛造前行》.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line02.cn: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 这里是《锻造前行》.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line03.en: Today, we'll discuss masonry building structures that stand the test of time.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line03.ch: 今天我們要聊石工, 蓋出經得起時間考驗的結構.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line03.cn: 今天我们要聊石工, 盖出经得起时间考验的结构.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line04.en: Bricks and mortar are the basics.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line04.ch: 磚塊和砂漿是最基本的東西.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line04.cn: 砖块和砂浆是最基本的东西.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line05.en: Mix sand, lime, and water to create mortar.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line05.ch: 把砂, 石灰和水混在一起, 就成了砂漿.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line05.cn: 把砂, 石灰和水混在一起, 就成了砂浆.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line06.en: Layer bricks with mortar to construct walls or repair existing ones.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line06.ch: 用砂漿把磚一層層砌起來, 就能蓋新牆或修補舊牆.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line06.cn: 用砂浆把砖一层层砌起来, 就能盖新墙或修补旧墙.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line07.ch: 每一層都要確認是水平的.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line07.cn: 每一层都要确认是水平的.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line08.en: Use a plumb line or a makeshift equivalent to keep your structure straight and stable.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line08.ch: 用鉛垂線, 或隨手做個替代品, 讓結構保持筆直穩固.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line08.cn: 用铅垂线, 或随手做个替代品, 让结构保持笔直稳固.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line09.en: Masonry adds durability to your defences.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line09.ch: 石工能讓你的防禦更耐久.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line09.cn: 石工能让你的防御更耐久.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line10.en: A well-built wall can provide safety against both the elements and unwanted guests.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line10.ch: 一道砌得好的牆, 既能擋風雨, 也能擋不速之客.
RM_ETC_FA5_Line10.cn: 一道砌得好的墙, 既能挡风雨, 也能挡不速之客.

RM_ETC_FA5_Line12.en: I'll see you next time on 'Forge Ahead.'

RM_ETC_FT1_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 槍械訓練 第1集
RM_ETC_FT1_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 枪械训练 第1集

RM_ETC_FT1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The distant sound of gunfire echoes softly.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_FT1_Line03.en: I'm Sergeant Davis, here to enhance your aiming skills.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line03.ch: 我是戴維斯中士, 這堂課要提升各位的瞄準能力.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line03.cn: 我是戴维斯中士, 这堂课要提升各位的瞄准能力.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line04.en: Proper aiming increases your accuracy, ensuring each shot counts.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line04.ch: 瞄準確實, 命中率就會提高, 每一發都不浪費.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line04.cn: 瞄准确实, 命中率就会提高, 每一发都不浪费.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line05.en: Always align your sights with the target, and maintain a steady stance to reduce recoil.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line05.ch: 準星務必對正目標, 站姿要穩, 才能減少後坐力.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line05.cn: 准星务必对正目标, 站姿要稳, 才能减少后坐力.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line06.en: One effective stance is the Weaver stance.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line06.ch: 其中一種有效的姿勢叫韋弗式站姿.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line06.cn: 其中一种有效的姿势叫韦弗式站姿.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line07.en: This provides greater stability and accuracy.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line07.ch: 它能提供更好的穩定性和精準度.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line07.cn: 它能提供更好的稳定性和精准度.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line08.en: Making it useful for shooting at multiple targets or when firing from behind cover.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line08.ch: 對付多個目標, 或是從掩體後射擊時特別好用.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line08.cn: 对付多个目标, 或是从掩体后射击时特别好用.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line10.en: The more you train, the more your accuracy, precision, and range improve.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line10.ch: 練得愈多, 命中率、精準度和射程都會跟著提升.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line10.cn: 练得越多, 命中率、精准度和射程都会跟着提升.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line11.en: Remember, firearms are tools of survival.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line11.ch: 記住, 槍械是求生的工具.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line11.cn: 记住, 枪械是求生的工具.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line12.ch: 明智使用, 負起責任.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line12.cn: 明智使用, 负起责任.

RM_ETC_FT1_Line13.en: Stay sharp, and join me next time on 'Firearms Training.'
RM_ETC_FT1_Line13.ch: 保持警覺, 我們《槍械訓練》下次見.
RM_ETC_FT1_Line13.cn: 保持警惕, 我们《枪械训练》下次见.

RM_ETC_FT1_Title.ch: 槍械訓練: 瞄準要領
RM_ETC_FT1_Title.cn: 枪械训练: 瞄准要领

RM_ETC_MW1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sound of tools clattering echoes through an empty garage.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_MW1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **工具的碰撞聲在空蕩蕩的車庫裡迴盪.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_MW1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **工具的碰撞声在空荡荡的车库里回荡.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_MW1_Line03.en: This is mechanics specialist Mike Carson with Vehicle Maintenance.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line03.ch: 我是技工專家麥克·卡森, 這集要講車輛保養.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line03.cn: 我是技工专家麦克·卡森, 这集要讲车辆保养.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line04.en: If you're hearing this, you've survived the initial outbreak in Knox County.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line04.ch: 如果你聽得到這段錄音, 代表你熬過了諾克斯縣最初的疫情爆發.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line04.cn: 如果你听得到这段录音, 代表你熬过了诺克斯县最初的疫情爆发.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line05.en: Your vehicle might be your only means of escape. Listen carefully.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line05.ch: 你的車可能是唯一的逃生工具. 仔細聽好.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line05.cn: 你的车可能是唯一的逃生工具. 仔细听好.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line06.en: Hot-wire only as a last resort.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line06.ch: 短接啟動只能當最後手段.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line06.cn: 短接启动只能当最后手段.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line08.en: Check glove compartments, homes, or nearby corpses.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line08.ch: 翻翻手套箱, 附近的住家, 或是屍體身上.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line08.cn: 翻翻手套箱, 附近的住家, 或是尸体身上.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line09.ch: 油箱隨時保持半滿以上.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line09.cn: 油箱随时保持半满以上.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line11.en: The power grid won't last forever.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line12.en: Check tire pressure and engine condition before any long journey. One breakdown could be fatal.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line12.ch: 長途出發前, 先檢查胎壓和引擎狀況. 拋錨一次就可能要命.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line12.cn: 长途出发前, 先检查胎压和引擎状况. 抛锚一次就可能要命.

RM_ETC_MW1_Line13.ch: 保持機動, 才活得下去.
RM_ETC_MW1_Line13.cn: 保持机动, 才活得下去.

RM_ETC_MW1_Title.ch: 技工工坊: 車輛保養
RM_ETC_MW1_Title.cn: 技工工坊: 车辆保养

RM_ETC_NP1_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 大自然的食物櫃 第1集
RM_ETC_NP1_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 大自然的食物柜 第1集

RM_ETC_NP1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The crunch of footsteps on leaves is faintly heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_NP1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **隱約傳來踩過落葉的沙沙腳步聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_NP1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **隐约传来踩过落叶的沙沙脚步声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_NP1_Line02.ch: 歡迎收看《大自然的食物櫃》.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line02.cn: 欢迎收看《大自然的食物柜》.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line03.en: I'm Alice, here to teach you how to eat from the land without eating poison.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line03.ch: 我是艾莉絲, 要教各位怎麼靠這片土地吃飯, 又不會把自己毒死.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line03.cn: 我是爱丽丝, 要教各位怎么靠这片土地吃饭, 又不会把自己毒死.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line04.en: Today, we're looking for wild berries.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來找野生漿果.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line04.cn: 今天我们要来找野生浆果.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line05.en: Blackberries and blueberries are your friends red or white berries? Probably not.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line05.ch: 黑莓和藍莓是你的好朋友, 至於紅色或白色的漿果呢? 大概就不是了.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line05.cn: 黑莓和蓝莓是你的好朋友, 至于红色或白色的浆果呢? 大概就不是了.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line06.en: Remember: if it's bitter, spit it out.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line06.ch: 記住: 嚐起來苦的, 就吐掉.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line06.cn: 记住: 尝起来苦的, 就吐掉.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line07.en: And always avoid mushrooms unless you're absolutely sure they're safe.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line07.ch: 還有, 蘑菇一律別碰, 除非你百分之百確定安全.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line07.cn: 还有, 蘑菇一律别碰, 除非你百分之百确定安全.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line08.en: Don't forget, nature has more than food.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line08.ch: 別忘了, 大自然給的不只是食物.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line08.cn: 别忘了, 大自然给的不只是食物.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line09.ch: 香蒲呢? 拿來當火種再好不過.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line09.cn: 香蒲呢? 拿来当火种再好不过.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line10.en: Pine needles? Brew them into tea for Vitamin C.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line10.ch: 松針呢? 泡成茶喝, 補充維他命 C.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line10.cn: 松针呢? 泡成茶喝, 补充维生素 C.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line11.ch: 各位, 在外頭要隨時提高警覺.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line11.cn: 各位, 在外头要随时提高警惕.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line12.en: Nature provides, but only if you know how to look.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line12.ch: 大自然什麼都有, 但前提是你得知道怎麼找.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line12.cn: 大自然什么都有, 但前提是你得知道怎么找.

RM_ETC_NP1_Line13.en: I'll see you next time on 'Nature's Pantry.'
RM_ETC_NP1_Line13.ch: 《大自然的食物櫃》, 我們下次見.
RM_ETC_NP1_Line13.cn: 《大自然的食物柜》, 我们下次见.

RM_ETC_NP1_Title.ch: 大自然的食物櫃: 野外採集求生
RM_ETC_NP1_Title.cn: 大自然的食物柜: 野外采集求生

RM_ETC_NP2_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 大自然的食物櫃 第2集
RM_ETC_NP2_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 大自然的食物柜 第2集

RM_ETC_NP2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The subtle sound of a knife being sharpened is heard.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_NP2_Line02.ch: 歡迎回到《大自然的食物櫃》.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line02.cn: 欢迎回到《大自然的食物柜》.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line03.en: I'm Alice, here to guide you through the essentials of butchering.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line03.ch: 我是艾莉絲, 今天要帶各位認識屠宰的基本功.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line03.cn: 我是爱丽丝, 今天要带各位认识屠宰的基本功.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line04.en: Proper butchering ensures you maximize the yield from your hunt, providing vital nutrition.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line04.ch: 手法正確, 才能把獵物的每一分都用上, 換來關鍵的營養.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line04.cn: 手法正确, 才能把猎物的每一分都用上, 换来关键的营养.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line05.en: Always start by ensuring your tools are clean and sharp.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line05.ch: 動手前, 一定要先確認工具乾淨又鋒利.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line05.cn: 动手前, 一定要先确认工具干净又锋利.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line06.en: Begin by making precise incisions along the joints to separate limbs.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line06.ch: 先沿著關節精準下刀, 把四肢卸下來.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line06.cn: 先沿着关节精准下刀, 把四肢卸下来.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line07.en: Then proceed to remove the hide carefully.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line07.ch: 接著小心地把毛皮剝下.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line07.cn: 接着小心地把毛皮剥下.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line08.en: Remember to separate the edible meat from organs and discard any parts that show signs of disease.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line08.ch: 記得把可食用的肉和內臟分開, 有病變跡象的部位一律丟掉.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line08.cn: 记得把可食用的肉和内脏分开, 有病变迹象的部位一律丢掉.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line10.en: If refrigeration isn't available, consider smoking or drying the meat.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line10.ch: 沒有冷藏設備的話, 可以考慮把肉煙燻或風乾.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line10.cn: 没有冷藏设备的话, 可以考虑把肉烟熏或风干.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line11.en: Stay safe, and respect the life that now sustains yours.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line11.ch: 注意安全, 也別忘了尊重這條供養你的生命.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line11.cn: 注意安全, 也别忘了尊重这条供养你的生命.

RM_ETC_NP2_Line12.ch: 《大自然的食物櫃》, 我們下次再會.
RM_ETC_NP2_Line12.cn: 《大自然的食物柜》, 我们下次再会.

RM_ETC_NP2_Title.ch: 大自然的食物櫃: 屠宰基本功
RM_ETC_NP2_Title.cn: 大自然的食物柜: 屠宰基本功

RM_ETC_NP3_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 大自然的食物櫃 第3集
RM_ETC_NP3_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 大自然的食物柜 第3集

RM_ETC_NP3_Line01.en: [img=music] **Soft sounds of animals rustling in the background.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_NP3_Line01.ch: [img=music] **背景傳來動物窸窸窣窣的輕響.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_NP3_Line01.cn: [img=music] **背景传来动物窸窸窣窣的轻响.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_NP3_Line02.en: Hello, survivors! I'm Alice, and this is 'Nature's Pantry.'
RM_ETC_NP3_Line02.ch: 哈囉, 各位倖存者! 我是艾莉絲, 這裡是《大自然的食物櫃》.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line02.cn: 各位幸存者, 大家好! 我是爱丽丝, 这里是《大自然的食物柜》.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line03.en: Today, we'll discuss basic animal care.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line03.ch: 今天我們要聊聊基本的動物照顧.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line03.cn: 今天我们要聊聊基本的动物照料.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line04.en: Domesticated animals can be a reliable food source, but they require proper care.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line04.ch: 家畜是很可靠的食物來源, 但前提是照顧得當.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line04.cn: 家畜是很可靠的食物来源, 但前提是照料得当.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line05.en: Ensure your animals have a clean shelter, access to fresh water, and a balanced diet.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line05.ch: 要確保牠們有乾淨的畜舍、喝得到乾淨的水, 還有均衡的飼料.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line05.cn: 要确保它们有干净的畜舍、喝得到干净的水, 还有均衡的饲料.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line06.en: Regularly check for signs of illness, such as changes in behavior or appearance.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line06.ch: 定期檢查有沒有生病的徵兆, 像是行為或外觀出現變化.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line06.cn: 定期检查有没有生病的征兆, 比如行为或外观出现变化.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line07.en: Healthy animals will provide you with meat, milk, eggs, and even companionship.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line07.ch: 健康的動物會回報你肉、奶、蛋, 甚至是陪伴.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line07.cn: 健康的动物会回报你肉、奶、蛋, 甚至是陪伴.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line08.en: Remember, their well-being directly affects your survival.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line08.ch: 記住, 牠們過得好不好, 直接關係到你能不能活下去.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line08.cn: 记住, 它们过得好不好, 直接关系到你能不能活下去.

RM_ETC_NP3_Line10.en: Stay tuned for more tips on 'Nature's Pantry.'
RM_ETC_NP3_Line10.ch: 《大自然的食物櫃》還有更多訣竅, 請繼續鎖定.
RM_ETC_NP3_Line10.cn: 《大自然的食物柜》还有更多窍门, 请继续锁定.

RM_ETC_NP3_Title.ch: 大自然的食物櫃: 動物照顧入門
RM_ETC_NP3_Title.cn: 大自然的食物柜: 动物照料入门

RM_ETC_NP4_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 大自然的食物櫃 第4集
RM_ETC_NP4_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 大自然的食物柜 第4集

RM_ETC_NP4_Line01.en: [img=music] **The gentle lapping of water against a boat is heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_NP4_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來水波輕輕拍打船身的聲音.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_NP4_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来水波轻轻拍打船身的声音.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_NP4_Line02.ch: 歡迎收看《大自然的食物櫃》.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line02.cn: 欢迎收看《大自然的食物柜》.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line03.en: I'm Alice, here to talk about fishing as a means of survival.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line03.ch: 我是艾莉絲, 今天要聊聊靠釣魚活下去這件事.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line03.cn: 我是爱丽丝, 今天要聊聊靠钓鱼活下去这件事.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line04.en: Rivers and lakes are abundant with fish, a great source of protein.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line04.ch: 河流和湖泊裡魚很多, 是很好的蛋白質來源.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line04.cn: 河流和湖泊里鱼很多, 是很好的蛋白质来源.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line05.en: Craft a simple fishing rod using a sturdy branch, some line, and a hook.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line05.ch: 找一根結實的樹枝, 加上釣線和魚鉤, 就能做出簡單的釣竿.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line05.cn: 找一根结实的树枝, 加上钓线和鱼钩, 就能做出简单的钓竿.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line06.en: Bait can be anything from worms to insects.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line06.ch: 餌料從蚯蚓到昆蟲都可以.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line06.cn: 饵料从蚯蚓到昆虫都可以.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line08.en: Always cook your catch thoroughly to avoid parasites.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line08.ch: 釣到的魚一定要煮到全熟, 才不會吃到寄生蟲.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line08.cn: 钓到的鱼一定要煮到全熟, 才不会吃到寄生虫.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line09.en: Fishing not only provides food but also a moment of peace in these trying times.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line09.ch: 釣魚不只帶來食物, 在這種艱難的日子裡, 還能換來片刻的平靜.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line09.cn: 钓鱼不只带来食物, 在这种艰难的日子里, 还能换来片刻的平静.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line10.ch: 注意安全, 祝各位釣得盡興.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line10.cn: 注意安全, 祝各位钓得尽兴.

RM_ETC_NP4_Line11.ch: 《大自然的食物櫃》, 我們下次再會.
RM_ETC_NP4_Line11.cn: 《大自然的食物柜》, 我们下次再会.

RM_ETC_NP4_Title.ch: 大自然的食物櫃: 釣魚求生
RM_ETC_NP4_Title.cn: 大自然的食物柜: 钓鱼求生

RM_ETC_NP5_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 大自然的食物櫃 第5集
RM_ETC_NP5_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 大自然的食物柜 第5集

RM_ETC_NP5_Line01.en: [img=music] **The faint snap of a trap being set is heard.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_NP5_Line02.en: Hello, I'm Alice, and welcome to 'Nature's Pantry.'
RM_ETC_NP5_Line02.ch: 哈囉, 我是艾莉絲, 歡迎收看《大自然的食物櫃》.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line02.cn: 大家好, 我是爱丽丝, 欢迎收看《大自然的食物柜》.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line03.en: Today, we'll cover basic trapping techniques.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line03.ch: 今天我們要講基本的陷阱技巧.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line03.cn: 今天我们要讲基本的陷阱技巧.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line04.en: Trapping is an efficient way to secure food without expending much energy.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line04.ch: 設陷阱很有效率, 不用花太多體力就能弄到食物.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line04.cn: 设陷阱很有效率, 不用花太多体力就能弄到食物.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line05.en: Start by identifying areas with high animal activity—tracks and droppings are good indicators.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line05.ch: 先找出動物活動頻繁的地方——足跡和糞便就是很好的線索.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line05.cn: 先找出动物活动频繁的地方——足迹和粪便就是很好的线索.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line06.en: Simple traps like snares can be made with minimal materials and set along animal paths.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line06.ch: 套索陷阱這類簡單的裝置, 用一點材料就能做, 架在獸徑上就行.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line06.cn: 套索陷阱这类简单的装置, 用一点材料就能做, 架在兽径上就行.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line07.en: Always check your traps regularly to ensure humane kills and prevent spoilage.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line07.ch: 陷阱一定要定期巡, 讓獵物少受折磨, 也避免肉放到壞掉.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line07.cn: 陷阱一定要定期巡, 让猎物少受折磨, 也避免肉放到坏掉.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line08.en: Remember, trapping requires patience and respect for wildlife.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line08.ch: 記住, 設陷阱靠的是耐心, 還有對野生動物的尊重.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line08.cn: 记住, 设陷阱靠的是耐心, 还有对野生动物的尊重.

RM_ETC_NP5_Line09.en: Stay resourceful, and see you next time on 'Nature's Pantry.'
RM_ETC_NP5_Line09.ch: 腦筋要靈活, 我們《大自然的食物櫃》下次見.
RM_ETC_NP5_Line09.cn: 脑筋要灵活, 我们《大自然的食物柜》下次见.

RM_ETC_NP5_Title.ch: 大自然的食物櫃: 陷阱技巧
RM_ETC_NP5_Title.cn: 大自然的食物柜: 陷阱技巧

RM_ETC_PU1_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 電力補給站 第1集
RM_ETC_PU1_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 电力补给站 第1集

RM_ETC_PU1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The faint ticking of a watch is heard, followed by a click.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來手錶細微的滴答聲, 接著是一聲喀噠.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来手表细微的滴答声, 接着是一声咔哒.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_PU1_Line03.en: I'm Sarah, here to guide you through salvaging electronics.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line03.ch: 我是莎拉, 今天要帶各位學怎麼回收電子零件.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line03.cn: 我是莎拉, 今天要带各位学怎么回收电子元件.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line04.en: Today, we'll dismantle digital watches for useful components.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line04.ch: 今天我們要拆電子錶, 取出有用的零件.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line04.cn: 今天我们要拆电子表, 取出有用的元件.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line05.en: Locate a digital watch common on the wrists of the deceased.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line05.ch: 先找一支電子錶, 死者的手腕上通常都有.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line05.cn: 先找一块电子表, 死者的手腕上通常都有.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line06.en: Carefully remove it to avoid damage.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line06.ch: 小心取下, 別弄壞了.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line06.cn: 小心取下, 别弄坏了.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line07.en: Using a small screwdriver or improvised tool, open the back panel to access the internal parts.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line07.ch: 用小螺絲起子或臨時湊合的工具, 打開錶背蓋, 就能碰到裡面的零件.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line07.cn: 用小螺丝刀或临时凑合的工具, 打开表背盖, 就能碰到里面的元件.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line08.en: Extract the battery and circuit board.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line09.en: These components are valuable for crafting and repairing electronic devices.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line09.ch: 這些零件在製作和修理電子裝置時非常寶貴.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line09.cn: 这些元件在制作和修理电子设备时非常宝贵.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line10.en: Remember, even the smallest parts can be crucial in survival situations.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line10.ch: 記住, 在求生的情況下, 再小的零件都可能是關鍵.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line10.cn: 记住, 在求生的情况下, 再小的元件都可能是关键.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line11.ch: 繼續收集, 繼續動手修.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line11.cn: 继续收集, 继续动手鼓捣.

RM_ETC_PU1_Line12.ch: 《電力補給站》, 我們下次見.
RM_ETC_PU1_Line12.cn: 《电力补给站》, 我们下次见.

RM_ETC_PU1_Title.ch: 電力補給站: 拆解手錶
RM_ETC_PU1_Title.cn: 电力补给站: 拆解手表

RM_ETC_PU2_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 電力補給站 第2集
RM_ETC_PU2_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 电力补给站 第2集

RM_ETC_PU2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The hum of a generator starting up fills the air.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **發電機啟動的嗡嗡聲充滿整個空間.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **发电机启动的嗡嗡声充满整个空间.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_PU2_Line02.ch: 各位倖存者好, 我是麗莎.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line02.cn: 各位幸存者好, 我是丽莎.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line03.en: Welcome to 'Power Up,' your guide to using generators safely and effectively.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line03.ch: 歡迎收看《電力補給站》, 帶你安全又有效率地使用發電機.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line03.cn: 欢迎收看《电力补给站》, 带你安全又有效率地使用发电机.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line04.en: Generators restore electricity to your home.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line04.ch: 發電機能讓你家重新有電.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line04.cn: 发电机能让你家重新有电.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line05.en: Place them outside to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning never indoors.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line05.ch: 一定要放在室外, 免得一氧化碳中毒——絕對不能放室內.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line05.cn: 一定要放在室外, 免得一氧化碳中毒——绝对不能放室内.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line06.en: Before connecting, ensure you have the necessary knowledge.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line06.ch: 接線之前, 先確定你有足夠的知識.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line06.cn: 接线之前, 先确定你有足够的知识.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line07.en: **Explains how to connect and use a generator**
RM_ETC_PU2_Line07.ch: **講解如何接上並操作發電機**
RM_ETC_PU2_Line07.cn: **讲解如何接上并操作发电机**

RM_ETC_PU2_Line09.en: Monitor consumption and turn off the generator when not in use to conserve resources.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line09.ch: 注意油耗, 不用的時候就把發電機關掉, 省著點用.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line09.cn: 注意油耗, 不用的时候就把发电机关掉, 省着点用.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line11.en: Check the condition and repair with spare parts as needed.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line11.ch: 檢查狀況, 必要時用備用零件修理.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line11.cn: 检查状况, 必要时用备用零件修理.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line12.ch: 保持供電, 保持準備.
RM_ETC_PU2_Line12.cn: 保持供电, 保持准备.

RM_ETC_PU2_Line13.en: Join me next time on 'Power Up.'

RM_ETC_PU2_Title.ch: 電力補給站: 安全使用發電機
RM_ETC_PU2_Title.cn: 电力补给站: 安全使用发电机

RM_ETC_PU3_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 電力補給站 第3集
RM_ETC_PU3_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 电力补给站 第3集

RM_ETC_PU3_Line01.en: [img=music] **The hum of a generator fades in, followed by a click.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU3_Line01.ch: [img=music] **發電機的嗡嗡聲漸漸浮現, 接著是一聲喀噠.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU3_Line01.cn: [img=music] **发电机的嗡嗡声渐渐浮现, 接着是一声咔哒.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_PU3_Line03.en: I'm Sarah, your guide to mastering electrical skills for survival.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line03.ch: 我是莎拉, 帶各位掌握求生必備的電工技能.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line03.cn: 我是莎拉, 带各位掌握求生必备的电工技能.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line04.en: Today, we'll cover the basics of electricity and essential safety precautions.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line04.ch: 今天我們要講電的基本原理, 還有一定要注意的安全事項.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line04.cn: 今天我们要讲电的基本原理, 还有一定要注意的安全事项.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line05.en: Electricity powers many of our essential tools, but it can be dangerous if mishandled.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line05.ch: 很多必需的工具都靠電運作, 但處理不當就會出事.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line05.cn: 很多必需的工具都靠电运行, 但处理不当就会出事.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line06.en: Always ensure the power source is turned off before working on any electrical components.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line06.ch: 動任何電子零件之前, 一定要先確認電源已經關掉.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line06.cn: 动任何电子元件之前, 一定要先确认电源已经关掉.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line07.en: Use insulated tools and wear rubber-soled shoes to reduce the risk of electric shock.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line07.ch: 使用絕緣工具, 穿橡膠底的鞋, 降低觸電的風險.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line07.cn: 使用绝缘工具, 穿橡胶底的鞋, 降低触电的风险.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line08.en: Familiarize yourself with basic electrical symbols and wiring diagrams to aid in repairs.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line08.ch: 熟悉基本的電路符號和配線圖, 修理時會輕鬆很多.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line08.cn: 熟悉基本的电路符号和接线图, 修理时会轻松很多.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line09.en: Remember, proper knowledge and caution are your best allies when working with electricity.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line09.ch: 記住, 跟電打交道, 正確的知識和謹慎就是你最好的夥伴.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line09.cn: 记住, 跟电打交道, 正确的知识和谨慎就是你最好的伙伴.

RM_ETC_PU3_Line10.en: Stay safe, stay powered, and join me next time on 'Power Up.'
RM_ETC_PU3_Line10.ch: 注意安全, 保持供電, 下次《電力補給站》再會.
RM_ETC_PU3_Line10.cn: 注意安全, 保持供电, 下次《电力补给站》再会.

RM_ETC_PU3_Title.en: Power Up: Electrical Safety and Basics
RM_ETC_PU3_Title.ch: 電力補給站: 用電安全與基礎
RM_ETC_PU3_Title.cn: 电力补给站: 用电安全与基础

RM_ETC_PU4_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 電力補給站 第4集
RM_ETC_PU4_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 电力补给站 第4集

RM_ETC_PU4_Line01.en: [img=music] **The distinctive crackle of radio frequency adjustment can be heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU4_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來調整無線電頻率時特有的沙沙雜訊.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PU4_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来调整无线电频率时特有的沙沙杂音.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_PU4_Line02.en: I'm Sarah, your guide to mastering electrical skills for survival.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line02.ch: 我是莎拉, 帶各位掌握求生必備的電工技能.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line02.cn: 我是莎拉, 带各位掌握求生必备的电工技能.

RM_ETC_PU4_Line03.en: Knox County's broadcast network is deteriorating. Listen carefully.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line03.ch: 諾克斯縣的廣播網正在崩壞. 仔細聽好.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line03.cn: 诺克斯县的广播网正在崩坏. 仔细听好.

RM_ETC_PU4_Line04.en: Your HAM radio is critical. Learn to wire it to car batteries for mobile operation.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line04.ch: 你的業餘無線電是關鍵. 學會把它接到汽車電池上, 就能帶著跑.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line04.cn: 你的业余无线电是关键. 学会把它接到汽车电池上, 就能带着跑.

RM_ETC_PU4_Line05.en: Automated stations are still broadcasting on emergency frequencies.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line05.ch: 自動電台仍在緊急頻率上播送.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line05.cn: 自动电台仍在紧急频率上播送.

RM_ETC_PU4_Line06.en: To maintain power, salvage electronic components from alarm clocks and televisions.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line06.ch: 要維持供電, 就從鬧鐘和電視機上拆電子零件.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line06.cn: 要维持供电, 就从闹钟和电视机上拆电子元件.

RM_ETC_PU4_Line07.en: Digital watches can provide crucial electrical parts for radio repair.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line07.ch: 電子錶能提供修理無線電時的關鍵電子零件.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line07.cn: 电子表能提供修理无线电时的关键电子元件.

RM_ETC_PU4_Line10.en: If you're hearing this, there are others out there.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line10.ch: 如果你聽得到這段話, 就表示外面還有其他人.
RM_ETC_PU4_Line10.cn: 如果你听得到这段话, 就表示外面还有其他人.

RM_ETC_PU4_Title.ch: 電力補給站: 緊急無線電作業
RM_ETC_PU4_Title.cn: 电力补给站: 紧急无线电作业

RM_ETC_PW1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The rhythmic sound of hands working wet clay can be heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PW1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **可以聽見雙手揉捏濕黏土的規律聲響.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_PW1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **可以听见双手揉捏湿黏土的规律声响.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_PW1_Line03.en: I'm Morgana, your guide to crafting with clay.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line03.ch: 我是摩根娜, 今天帶各位用黏土做東西.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line03.cn: 我是摩根娜, 今天带各位用黏土做东西.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line04.en: In a world without refrigeration, preserving food is vital.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line04.ch: 在一個沒有冷藏的世界裡, 保存食物非常重要.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line04.cn: 在一个没有冷藏的世界里, 保存食物非常重要.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line05.en: Today, we're making clay storage containers from local soil.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line05.ch: 今天我們要就地取土, 做黏土儲物容器.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line05.cn: 今天我们要就地取土, 做黏土储物容器.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line07.en: Creek beds are ideal. Avoid contaminated areas.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line07.ch: 溪床最理想. 避開受汙染的區域.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line07.cn: 溪床最理想. 避开受污染的区域.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line08.en: Mix with water until it holds shape.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line10.en: Shape into containers. Thicker walls last longer.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line10.ch: 捏成容器. 壁厚一點比較耐用.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line10.cn: 捏成容器. 壁厚一点比较耐用.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line11.en: Let dry in shade. Sun-drying causes cracks.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line11.ch: 放陰涼處陰乾. 曝曬會裂.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line11.cn: 放阴凉处阴干. 曝晒会裂.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line12.en: Fire in a covered pit to avoid smoke.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line12.ch: 在有蓋的坑裡燒製, 才不會冒煙.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line12.cn: 在有盖的坑里烧制, 才不会冒烟.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line13.en: Use for dry goods storage. Root vegetables. Seeds.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line13.ch: 拿來裝乾貨. 根莖類蔬菜. 種子.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line13.cn: 拿来装干货. 根茎类蔬菜. 种子.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line14.ch: 繼續動手做, 撐下去.
RM_ETC_PW1_Line14.cn: 继续动手做, 撑下去.

RM_ETC_PW1_Line15.en: See you next time on 'Pottery Workshop.'

RM_ETC_PW1_Title.ch: 陶藝工坊: 製作黏土容器
RM_ETC_PW1_Title.cn: 陶艺工坊: 制作黏土容器

RM_ETC_SA1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sound of a medical kit unzipping plays softly.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SA1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **輕輕傳來急救包拉鍊拉開的聲音.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SA1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **轻轻传来急救包拉链拉开的声音.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SA1_Line02.en: Hi, I'm Dr. Lewis, and this is 'Stay Alive.'
RM_ETC_SA1_Line02.ch: 你好, 我是路易斯醫師, 這裡是《活下去》.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line02.cn: 你好, 我是刘易斯医生, 这里是《活下去》.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line03.en: Let's talk about first aid when every second counts.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line03.ch: 我們來聊聊分秒必爭時的急救.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line03.cn: 我们来聊聊分秒必争时的急救.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line04.en: Got a deep cut? Apply pressure to stop the bleeding.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line04.ch: 傷口很深嗎? 加壓止血.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line04.cn: 伤口很深吗? 加压止血.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line05.en: No clean cloth? Boil it first if you can it'll save you from infection.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line05.ch: 沒有乾淨的布? 有辦法的話先煮過——這能讓你免於感染.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line05.cn: 没有干净的布? 有办法的话先煮过——这能让你免于感染.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line06.en: For burns, cool water is your best friend.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line06.ch: 燒燙傷的話, 冷水是你最好的朋友.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line06.cn: 烧烫伤的话, 凉水是你最好的朋友.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line07.en: Never use ice it'll make it worse.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line07.ch: 千萬別用冰塊——只會更糟.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line07.cn: 千万别用冰块——只会更糟.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line08.ch: 還有記住: 傷口不處理, 是會要命的.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line08.cn: 还有记住: 伤口不处理, 是会要命的.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line09.en: Clean, bandage, and keep it dry.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line09.ch: 清潔, 包紮, 保持乾燥.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line09.cn: 清洁, 包扎, 保持干燥.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line10.ch: 活下去, 就從這些基本功開始.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line10.cn: 活下去, 就从这些基本功开始.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line11.en: Stay sharp, stay prepared, and stay alive.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line11.ch: 保持警覺, 保持準備, 活下去.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line11.cn: 保持警惕, 保持准备, 活下去.

RM_ETC_SA1_Line12.en: This is Dr. Lewis, signing off.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line12.ch: 我是路易斯醫師, 我們下次再會.
RM_ETC_SA1_Line12.cn: 我是刘易斯医生, 我们下次再会.

RM_ETC_SA1_Title.ch: 活下去: 緊急醫療處置
RM_ETC_SA1_Title.cn: 活下去: 紧急医疗处置

RM_ETC_SA2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The soft beeping of medical equipment plays in the background.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SA2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **背景傳來醫療儀器輕輕的嗶嗶聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SA2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **背景传来医疗仪器轻轻的哔哔声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SA2_Line02.en: Hi, I'm Dr. Lewis, and this is 'Stay Alive.'
RM_ETC_SA2_Line02.ch: 你好, 我是路易斯醫師, 這裡是《活下去》.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line02.cn: 你好, 我是刘易斯医生, 这里是《活下去》.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line03.en: Today, we'll discuss recognizing and treating hypothermia.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line03.ch: 今天我們要談怎麼辨識和處理失溫.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line03.cn: 今天我们要谈怎么辨识和处理失温.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line04.en: Early signs include shivering, confusion, and slurred speech.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line04.ch: 早期徵兆包括發抖、意識混亂, 還有口齒不清.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line04.cn: 早期征兆包括发抖、意识混乱, 还有口齿不清.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line05.en: If untreated, it can lead to unconsciousness.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line05.ch: 不處理的話, 可能會失去意識.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line05.cn: 不处理的话, 可能会失去意识.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line06.en: Move the person to a warm area.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line07.en: Remove any wet clothing and cover them with blankets.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line07.ch: 脫掉所有濕掉的衣物, 蓋上毯子.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line07.cn: 脱掉所有湿掉的衣物, 盖上毯子.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line08.en: Offer warm liquids if they're conscious.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line08.ch: 如果人還清醒, 給他喝點溫熱的飲品.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line08.cn: 如果人还清醒, 给他喝点温热的饮品.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line10.en: Stay dry, stay warm, and stay alive.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line10.ch: 保持乾燥, 保持溫暖, 活下去.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line10.cn: 保持干燥, 保持温暖, 活下去.

RM_ETC_SA2_Line11.en: Join me next time for more survival medical tips.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line11.ch: 下次再一起看更多求生醫療訣竅.
RM_ETC_SA2_Line11.cn: 下次再一起看更多求生医疗窍门.

RM_ETC_SA2_Title.ch: 活下去: 失溫的處理
RM_ETC_SA2_Title.cn: 活下去: 失温的处理

RM_ETC_SA3_Line01.en: [img=music] **The muffled sound of a medical mask being adjusted is heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SA3_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來調整口罩時悶悶的摩擦聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SA3_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来调整口罩时闷闷的摩擦声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SA3_Line02.en: Hello survivors, I'm Dr. Robert Lewis, and welcome back to 'Stay Alive.'
RM_ETC_SA3_Line02.ch: 各位倖存者好, 我是羅伯特·路易斯醫師, 歡迎回到《活下去》.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line02.cn: 各位幸存者好, 我是罗伯特·刘易斯医生, 欢迎回到《活下去》.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line03.en: Today, we're discussing the dangers of corpse sickness and the importance of respiratory protection.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line03.ch: 今天我們要談屍臭病的危害, 以及呼吸道防護的重要性.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line03.cn: 今天我们要谈尸臭病的危害, 以及呼吸道防护的重要性.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line04.en: In the aftermath of the Knox Event, decaying bodies pose serious health risks.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line04.ch: 諾克斯事件之後, 腐爛的屍體帶來嚴重的健康風險.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line04.cn: 诺克斯事件之后, 腐烂的尸体带来严重的健康风险.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line05.en: Prolonged exposure can lead to queasiness, severe illness, and even death.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line05.ch: 長時間暴露會引起噁心反胃、重病, 甚至死亡.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line05.cn: 长时间暴露会引起恶心反胃、重病, 甚至死亡.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line06.en: If you notice a queasy feeling after being near corpses, it's a warning sign.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line06.ch: 如果靠近屍體之後覺得反胃, 那就是警訊.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line06.cn: 如果靠近尸体之后觉得反胃, 那就是警讯.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line07.en: Distance yourself immediately and seek fresh air to prevent the condition from worsening.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line07.ch: 立刻拉開距離, 去呼吸新鮮空氣, 免得情況惡化.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line07.cn: 立刻拉开距离, 去呼吸新鲜空气, 免得情况恶化.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line08.en: Wearing masks can help reduce the risk.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line09.en: While medical-grade masks are ideal, homemade respirators can offer some protection.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line09.ch: 醫療級口罩當然最理想, 但自製的呼吸面罩也能提供一定的保護.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line09.cn: 医疗级口罩当然最理想, 但自制的呼吸面罩也能提供一定的保护.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line10.en: Craft one using materials like cloth and activated charcoal.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line10.ch: 用布料和活性炭這類材料就能做出一個.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line10.cn: 用布料和活性炭这类材料就能做出一个.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line11.en: Remember, maintaining distance from decaying bodies and using respiratory protection are key to staying healthy in these trying times.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line11.ch: 記住, 在這種艱難的日子裡, 遠離腐屍加上呼吸道防護, 就是保持健康的關鍵.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line11.cn: 记住, 在这种艰难的日子里, 远离腐尸加上呼吸道防护, 就是保持健康的关键.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line12.en: Stay vigilant, stay protected, and as always, stay alive.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line12.ch: 保持警戒, 做好防護, 還有一如既往, 活下去.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line12.cn: 保持警戒, 做好防护, 还有一如既往, 活下去.

RM_ETC_SA3_Line13.en: This is Dr. Lewis, signing off.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line13.ch: 我是路易斯醫師, 我們下次再會.
RM_ETC_SA3_Line13.cn: 我是刘易斯医生, 我们下次再会.

RM_ETC_SA3_Title.en: Stay Alive: Understanding Corpse Sickness and Respiratory Protection
RM_ETC_SA3_Title.ch: 活下去: 認識屍臭病與呼吸道防護
RM_ETC_SA3_Title.cn: 活下去: 认识尸臭病与呼吸道防护

RM_ETC_SW1_ItemDisplayName.en: VHS: Signs in the Wild E1

RM_ETC_SW1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The soft whistle of wind through trees plays.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **風穿過樹梢, 發出輕柔的呼嘯.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **风穿过树梢, 发出轻柔的呼啸.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SW1_Line02.en: Hey there, I'm Jack, and welcome to 'Signs in the Wild.'
RM_ETC_SW1_Line02.ch: 嘿, 大家好, 我是傑克, 歡迎收看《荒野蹤跡》.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line02.cn: 嘿, 大家好, 我是杰克, 欢迎收看《荒野踪迹》.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line03.en: Let's learn to see what the forest wants to tell us.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line03.ch: 今天我們來學怎麼看懂森林想告訴我們的事.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line03.cn: 今天我们来学怎么看懂森林想告诉我们的事.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line05.en: Look for deer they mean water and safety.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line05.ch: 找鹿的足跡, 有鹿就代表有水, 也代表安全.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line05.cn: 找鹿的足迹, 有鹿就代表有水, 也代表安全.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line06.en: Human tracks? Be careful might not be friendly.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line06.ch: 人的足跡呢? 那要小心了, 對方不見得是善類.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line06.cn: 人的足迹呢? 那要小心了, 对方不见得是善类.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line07.en: Broken branches or trampled grass can point the way.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line07.ch: 折斷的樹枝, 被踩倒的草, 都能替你指路.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line07.cn: 折断的树枝, 被踩倒的草, 都能替你指路.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line08.en: Nature leaves clues learn to read them.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line08.ch: 大自然會留下線索, 學著把它們讀懂.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line08.cn: 大自然会留下线索, 学着把它们读懂.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line09.en: Need to find north? Moss grows thicker on the north side of trees.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line09.ch: 要找北方? 樹幹北面的苔蘚長得比較厚.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line09.cn: 要找北方? 树干北面的苔藓长得比较厚.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line10.en: And the sun always rises in the east, sets in the west.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line10.ch: 還有, 太陽永遠東升西落.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line10.cn: 还有, 太阳永远东升西落.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line11.en: Keep your eyes open, your steps quiet, and your mind sharp.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line11.ch: 眼睛放亮, 腳步放輕, 腦袋放清楚.
RM_ETC_SW1_Line11.cn: 眼睛放亮, 脚步放轻, 脑袋放清楚.

RM_ETC_SW1_Line12.en: See you next time on 'Signs in the Wild.'

RM_ETC_SW1_Title.en: Signs in the Wild: Tracking and Navigation
RM_ETC_SW1_Title.ch: 荒野蹤跡: 追蹤與辨向
RM_ETC_SW1_Title.cn: 荒野踪迹: 追踪与辨向

RM_ETC_SW2_ItemDisplayName.en: VHS: Signs in the Wild E2

RM_ETC_SW2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The faint sound of branches snapping and leaves rustling sets the scene.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **隱約傳來樹枝折斷與落葉沙沙的聲響.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **隐约传来树枝折断与落叶沙沙的声响.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SW2_Line02.en: Hey there, I'm Jack, and welcome to 'Signs in the Wild.'
RM_ETC_SW2_Line02.ch: 嘿, 大家好, 我是傑克, 歡迎收看《荒野蹤跡》.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line02.cn: 嘿, 大家好, 我是杰克, 欢迎收看《荒野踪迹》.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line03.en: Today, we'll learn to construct a simple lean-to shelter.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line03.ch: 今天我們要學怎麼搭一座簡易的斜頂庇護所.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line03.cn: 今天我们要学怎么搭一座简易的斜顶庇护所.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line04.en: Find a downed tree or place a sturdy branch between two supports.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line04.ch: 找一根倒木, 或者在兩個支點之間架上一根結實的樹枝.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line04.cn: 找一根倒木, 或者在两个支点之间架上一根结实的树枝.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line05.en: Lean smaller branches against it to form a frame.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line05.ch: 把比較小的樹枝斜靠上去, 做出骨架.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line05.cn: 把比较小的树枝斜靠上去, 做出骨架.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line06.en: Cover the frame with leaves or moss to provide insulation and camouflage.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line06.ch: 再用樹葉或苔蘚把骨架蓋滿, 既能保暖, 又能偽裝.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line06.cn: 再用树叶或苔藓把骨架盖满, 既能保暖, 又能伪装.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line07.en: This shelter offers protection from the elements.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line07.ch: 這種庇護所能替你擋掉風吹雨打.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line07.cn: 这种庇护所能替你挡掉风吹雨打.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line08.en: Survival often depends on quick thinking and adaptability.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line08.ch: 能不能活下來, 往往就看你反應夠不夠快, 夠不夠隨機應變.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line08.cn: 能不能活下来, 往往就看你反应够不够快, 够不够随机应变.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line09.ch: 多練幾次, 隨時做好準備.
RM_ETC_SW2_Line09.cn: 多练几次, 随时做好准备.

RM_ETC_SW2_Line10.en: See you next time on 'Signs in the Wild.'

RM_ETC_SW2_Title.en: Signs in the Wild: Building Emergency Shelters
RM_ETC_SW2_Title.ch: 荒野蹤跡: 搭建緊急庇護所
RM_ETC_SW2_Title.cn: 荒野踪迹: 搭建紧急庇护所

RM_ETC_SW3_ItemDisplayName.en: VHS: Signs in the Wild E3

RM_ETC_SW3_Line01.en: [img=music] **The soft scrape of a knife against wood is heard.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW3_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來刀刃輕輕刮過木頭的聲音.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW3_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来刀刃轻轻刮过木头的声音.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SW3_Line02.en: Welcome back to 'Signs in the Wild.'

RM_ETC_SW3_Line03.en: I'm Jack, your guide to wilderness skills.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line03.ch: 我是傑克, 帶各位認識荒野技能.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line03.cn: 我是杰克, 带各位认识荒野技能.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line04.en: Today, we'll cover carving tools for survival.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來講怎麼雕出求生用的工具.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line04.cn: 今天我们要来讲怎么雕出求生用的工具.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line05.en: A simple spear can be your best friend.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line05.ch: 一根簡單的長矛, 就可能是你最好的朋友.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line05.cn: 一根简单的长矛, 就可能是你最好的朋友.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line06.en: Find a straight branch, about as tall as you.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line06.ch: 找一根筆直的樹枝, 大概跟你一樣高.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line06.cn: 找一根笔直的树枝, 大概跟你一样高.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line07.en: Use your knife to sharpen one end to a point.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line08.ch: 把矛尖用火烤硬, 可以更耐用.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line08.cn: 把矛尖用火烤硬, 可以更耐用.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line09.en: Hold the point over hot coals not flames until it darkens.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line09.ch: 把尖端拿到炭火上方烤, 不是火焰上, 烤到顏色變深為止.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line09.cn: 把尖端拿到炭火上方烤, 不是火焰上, 烤到颜色变深为止.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line10.ch: 這樣木頭就會變得更堅韌.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line10.cn: 这样木头就会变得更坚韧.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line11.en: Always carve away from yourself to avoid injury.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line11.ch: 刀鋒一定要往外削, 才不會傷到自己.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line11.cn: 刀锋一定要往外削, 才不会伤到自己.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line12.en: A slip can cost you more than time out here.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line12.ch: 在這種地方手一滑, 賠掉的可不只是時間.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line12.cn: 在这种地方手一滑, 赔掉的可不只是时间.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line13.en: With practice, you'll craft tools that make survival easier.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line13.ch: 多練幾次, 你就能做出讓求生輕鬆許多的工具.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line13.cn: 多练几次, 你就能做出让求生轻松许多的工具.

RM_ETC_SW3_Line14.en: Stay tuned for more on 'Signs in the Wild.'
RM_ETC_SW3_Line14.ch: 《荒野蹤跡》還有更多內容, 別轉台.
RM_ETC_SW3_Line14.cn: 《荒野踪迹》还有更多内容, 别换台.

RM_ETC_SW4_ItemDisplayName.en: VHS: Signs in the Wild E4

RM_ETC_SW4_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sharp crack of stone striking stone echoes softly.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW4_Line01.ch: [img=music] **石頭撞擊石頭的清脆聲響輕輕迴盪.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_SW4_Line01.cn: [img=music] **石头撞击石头的清脆声响轻轻回荡.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_SW4_Line02.en: Hello, survivors. Jack here with 'Signs in the Wild.'
RM_ETC_SW4_Line02.ch: 各位倖存者好. 我是傑克, 這裡是《荒野蹤跡》.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line02.cn: 各位幸存者好. 我是杰克, 这里是《荒野踪迹》.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line03.en: Let's delve into knapping turning stone into essential tools.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line03.ch: 今天我們深入聊聊打石術, 把石頭變成不可或缺的工具.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line03.cn: 今天我们深入聊聊打石术, 把石头变成不可或缺的工具.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line04.en: Find a hard, brittle rock like flint or chert.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line04.ch: 先找一塊又硬又脆的石頭, 像燧石或矽質岩.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line04.cn: 先找一块又硬又脆的石头, 像燧石或硅质岩.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line05.en: Strike it with a hammerstone to chip off flakes, creating a sharp edge.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line05.ch: 用錘石敲它, 敲下石片, 就能敲出鋒利的刃口.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line05.cn: 用锤石敲它, 敲下石片, 就能敲出锋利的刃口.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line06.ch: 接著用壓剝法把刃口修得更細.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line06.cn: 接着用压剥法把刃口修得更细.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line07.en: Use a bone or antler to press small flakes from the tool, sharpening it further.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line07.ch: 拿一塊骨頭或鹿角, 從工具上壓下細小的石片, 讓它更鋒利.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line07.cn: 拿一块骨头或鹿角, 从工具上压下细小的石片, 让它更锋利.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line08.en: Knapped tools can serve as knives or arrowheads.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line08.ch: 打製出來的石器可以當刀子, 也可以當箭頭.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line08.cn: 打制出来的石器可以当刀子, 也可以当箭头.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line09.en: In a pinch, they're invaluable for hunting and crafting.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line09.ch: 情況緊急的時候, 它們在狩獵和製作上都是無價之寶.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line09.cn: 情况紧急的时候, 它们在狩猎和制作上都是无价之宝.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line10.en: Master this skill, and the wilderness offers more than threats it offers solutions.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line10.ch: 把這門技術練熟, 荒野給你的就不只是威脅, 還有解答.
RM_ETC_SW4_Line10.cn: 把这门技术练熟, 荒野给你的就不只是威胁, 还有解答.

RM_ETC_SW4_Line11.en: Until next time on 'Signs in the Wild.'

RM_ETC_TS1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The faint sound of scissors cutting fabric plays.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_TS1_Line02.en: Hey there, I'm Karen, and welcome to 'Thread for Survival,'.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line02.ch: 嘿, 大家好, 我是凱倫, 歡迎收看《一線生機》.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line02.cn: 嘿, 大家好, 我是凯伦, 欢迎收看《一线生机》.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line03.en: Where we turn rags into riches or at least something wearable.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line03.ch: 在這裡, 我們把破布變黃金, 至少變成能穿的東西.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line03.cn: 在这里, 我们把破布变黄金, 至少变成能穿的东西.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line04.en: Today, we'll patch those jeans you've been wearing for days.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來補那件你穿了好幾天的牛仔褲.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line04.cn: 今天我们要来补那条你穿了好几天的牛仔裤.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line05.en: First, find some sturdy fabric old curtains or even a couch will do.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line05.ch: 首先, 找點結實的布料, 舊窗簾, 甚至沙發套都可以.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line05.cn: 首先, 找点结实的布料, 旧窗帘, 甚至沙发套都可以.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line06.en: No thread? No problem! Use fishing line or dental floss.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line06.ch: 沒有線? 沒問題! 拿魚線或牙線來用.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line06.cn: 没有线? 没问题! 拿鱼线或牙线来用.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line07.en: It's strong and gets the job done.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line07.ch: 又牢固, 又能把事情辦好.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line07.cn: 又牢固, 又能把事情办好.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line08.en: When sewing by hand, remember: small stitches are stronger.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line08.ch: 手縫的時候記住: 針腳越小越牢.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line08.cn: 手缝的时候记住: 针脚越小越牢.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line09.en: Take your time this isn't a fashion show, it's survival.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line09.ch: 慢慢來, 這又不是時裝秀, 這是求生.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line09.cn: 慢慢来, 这又不是时装秀, 这是求生.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line10.en: Clothes aren't just comfort. They're protection.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line10.ch: 衣服不只是為了舒服. 它是保護.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line10.cn: 衣服不只是为了舒服. 它是保护.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line11.en: Keep them patched, keep them clean, and they'll keep you alive.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line11.ch: 勤補, 勤洗, 它們就會讓你活下去.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line11.cn: 勤补, 勤洗, 它们就会让你活下去.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line12.en: Thanks for tuning in to 'Thread for Survival.'
RM_ETC_TS1_Line12.ch: 感謝各位收看《一線生機》.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line12.cn: 感谢各位收看《一线生机》.

RM_ETC_TS1_Line13.ch: 針線別放下, 命也別放下.
RM_ETC_TS1_Line13.cn: 针线别放下, 命也别放下.

RM_ETC_TS1_Title.en: Thread for Survival: Emergency Clothing Repairs
RM_ETC_TS1_Title.ch: 一線生機: 緊急衣物修補
RM_ETC_TS1_Title.cn: 一线生机: 紧急衣物修补

RM_ETC_TS2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sound of pages flipping is followed by tearing paper.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_TS2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **先是翻頁的聲音, 接著是撕紙聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_TS2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **先是翻页的声音, 接着是撕纸声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_TS2_Line03.en: I'm Karen, here to share tips on improvised protection.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line03.ch: 我是凱倫, 今天要跟各位分享臨時防護的訣竅.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line03.cn: 我是凯伦, 今天要跟各位分享临时防护的诀窍.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line04.en: Today, we'll craft magazine armour for your limbs.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line04.ch: 今天我們要用雜誌做四肢的護具.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line04.cn: 今天我们要用杂志做四肢的护具.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line05.en: Gather several magazines these will serve as the protective layer against bites and scratches.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line05.ch: 先收集幾本雜誌, 它們就是擋咬傷和抓傷的防護層.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line05.cn: 先收集几本杂志, 它们就是挡咬伤和抓伤的防护层.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line06.en: Secure the magazines around your forearms and shins using duct tape or cloth strips.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line06.ch: 用大力膠帶或布條, 把雜誌固定在前臂和小腿上.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line06.cn: 用管道胶带或布条, 把杂志固定在前臂和小腿上.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line07.en: Ensure they're snug but not restrictive.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line07.ch: 要綁得貼身, 但不能綁到動不了.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line07.cn: 要绑得贴身, 但不能绑到动不了.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line08.en: This makeshift armour can significantly reduce injury from close encounters with the infected.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line08.ch: 這種臨時護具, 能大幅減少和感染者近距離接觸時受的傷.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line08.cn: 这种临时护具, 能大幅减少和感染者近距离接触时受的伤.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line09.ch: 多動點腦筋, 保護好自己.
RM_ETC_TS2_Line09.cn: 多动点脑筋, 保护好自己.

RM_ETC_TS2_Line10.en: Until next time on 'Thread for Survival.'

RM_ETC_TS2_Title.en: Thread for Survival: Crafting Protective Gear
RM_ETC_TS2_Title.ch: 一線生機: 自製防護裝備
RM_ETC_TS2_Title.cn: 一线生机: 自制防护装备

RM_ETC_VG1_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 勝利菜園 第1集
RM_ETC_VG1_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 胜利菜园 第1集

RM_ETC_VG1_Line01.en: [img=music] **Soft sounds of a shovel digging in dirt.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_VG1_Line02.en: Hello, survivors! I'm Pythia, and this is 'Victory Gardens,'
RM_ETC_VG1_Line02.ch: 哈囉, 各位倖存者! 我是皮媞亞, 這裡是《勝利菜園》,
RM_ETC_VG1_Line02.cn: 各位幸存者, 大家好! 我是皮媞亚, 这里是《胜利菜园》,

RM_ETC_VG1_Line03.en: Your guide to growing food when grocery stores are a memory.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line03.ch: 在雜貨店只剩回憶的年代, 帶你自己種出食物.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line03.cn: 在杂货店只剩回忆的年代, 带你自己种出食物.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來種馬鈴薯.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line05.en: They're hardy, filling, and don't need much attention perfect survival food.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line05.ch: 它們耐命、有飽足感, 又不太需要照顧——根本是完美的求生糧食.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line05.cn: 它们皮实、顶饱, 又不太需要照料——根本是完美的求生粮食.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line06.en: Cut a potato into chunks with at least one 'eye' on each piece.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line06.ch: 把馬鈴薯切塊, 每塊至少要留一個「芽眼」.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line06.cn: 把土豆切块, 每块至少要留一个“芽眼”.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line07.en: Bury them a few inches deep and keep the soil moist.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line07.ch: 埋進土裡幾英吋深, 並保持土壤濕潤.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line07.cn: 埋进土里几英寸深, 并保持土壤湿润.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line08.en: No fertiliser? No problem! Compost scraps like eggshells, coffee grounds, and leaves.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line08.ch: 沒有肥料? 沒問題! 把蛋殼、咖啡渣和落葉這些廚餘拿去做堆肥.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line08.cn: 没有肥料? 没问题! 把蛋壳、咖啡渣和落叶这些厨余拿去做堆肥.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line10.en: Remember, every plant you grow is a step closer to survival.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line10.ch: 記住, 你種下的每一株, 都讓你離活下去更近一步.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line10.cn: 记住, 你种下的每一株, 都让你离活下去更近一步.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line11.en: Keep planting, keep eating, and keep striving for better.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line11.ch: 繼續種, 繼續吃, 繼續往更好的日子前進.
RM_ETC_VG1_Line11.cn: 继续种, 继续吃, 继续往更好的日子前进.

RM_ETC_VG1_Line12.en: See you next time on 'Victory Gardens.'

RM_ETC_VG1_Title.en: Victory Gardens: A Modern Guide to Self-Sufficiency
RM_ETC_VG1_Title.ch: 勝利菜園: 自給自足的現代指南
RM_ETC_VG1_Title.cn: 胜利菜园: 自给自足的现代指南

RM_ETC_VG2_ItemDisplayName.ch: VHS: 勝利菜園 第2集
RM_ETC_VG2_ItemDisplayName.cn: VHS: 胜利菜园 第2集

RM_ETC_VG2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The gentle rustling of soil being poured into a container is audible.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_VG2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **可以聽見土壤緩緩倒進容器的沙沙聲.** [img=music]
RM_ETC_VG2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **可以听见土壤缓缓倒进容器的沙沙声.** [img=music]

RM_ETC_VG2_Line03.en: I'm Pythia, and this is 'Victory Gardens,' your guide to sustainable living.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line03.ch: 我是皮媞亞, 這裡是《勝利菜園》, 帶你走向自給自足的生活.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line03.cn: 我是皮媞亚, 这里是《胜利菜园》, 带你走向自给自足的生活.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line04.en: Today, we'll explore container gardening perfect for those without access to open ground.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來聊容器種菜——沒有一塊空地的人最適合.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line04.cn: 今天我们要来聊容器种菜——没有一块空地的人最适合.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line05.en: Ensure your containers have drainage holes to prevent waterlogging.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line05.ch: 記得在容器上留排水孔, 免得積水爛根.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line05.cn: 记得在容器上留排水孔, 免得积水烂根.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line06.en: Place them in areas with ample sunlight.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line07.en: Use buckets, tubs, or even old tyres filled with soil.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line07.ch: 水桶、澡盆, 甚至舊輪胎裝滿土都可以.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line07.cn: 水桶、盆子, 甚至旧轮胎装满土都可以.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line08.en: Plant fast-growing crops like lettuce or radishes for quick harvests.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line08.ch: 種生菜或櫻桃蘿蔔這種長得快的作物, 很快就能收成.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line08.cn: 种生菜或樱桃萝卜这种长得快的作物, 很快就能收获.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line09.ch: 記住, 懂得就地取材, 才撐得久.
RM_ETC_VG2_Line09.cn: 记住, 懂得就地取材, 才撑得久.

RM_ETC_VG2_Line10.en: Keep Sowing and Build your future!
RM_ETC_VG2_Line10.ch: 繼續播種, 親手打造你的未來!
RM_ETC_VG2_Line10.cn: 继续播种, 亲手打造你的未来!

RM_ETC_VG2_Line11.en: See you next time on 'Victory Gardens.'

RM_ETC_VG2_Title.ch: 勝利菜園: 容器種菜
RM_ETC_VG2_Title.cn: 胜利菜园: 容器种菜

ETC_FA1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sound of metal clanging echoes faintly in the background.** [img=music]
ETC_FA1_Line01.ch: [img=music] **背景隱約迴盪著金屬敲擊的聲響.** [img=music]
ETC_FA1_Line01.cn: [img=music] **背景隐约回荡着金属敲击的声响.** [img=music]

ETC_FA1_Line02.en: Welcome to 'Forge Ahead,' your guide to survival crafting.
ETC_FA1_Line02.ch: 歡迎收看《鍛造前行》, 你的求生製作指南.
ETC_FA1_Line02.cn: 欢迎收看《锻造前行》, 你的求生制作指南.

ETC_FA1_Line03.en: I'm Rick, a former army engineer, here to help you turn scraps into survival tools.
ETC_FA1_Line03.ch: 我是瑞克, 以前是陸軍工兵, 今天要教各位把廢料變成求生工具.
ETC_FA1_Line03.cn: 我是瑞克, 以前是陆军工兵, 今天要教各位把废料变成求生工具.

ETC_FA1_Line04.en: Today, we'll learn how to make a basic barricade using salvaged sheet metal.
ETC_FA1_Line04.ch: 今天我們要來學怎麼用撿回來的金屬板做一道簡易路障.
ETC_FA1_Line04.cn: 今天我们要来学怎么用捡回来的金属板做一道简易路障.

ETC_FA1_Line05.en: First, look for old appliances or wrecked vehicles they're treasure troves.
ETC_FA1_Line05.ch: 首先, 去找老舊家電或報廢車輛, 那些都是寶庫.
ETC_FA1_Line05.cn: 首先, 去找老旧家电或报废车辆, 那些都是宝库.

ETC_FA1_Line06.en: To shape the metal, you'll need a hammer or a sturdy rock.
ETC_FA1_Line06.ch: 要把金屬敲成形, 你需要一把鎚子, 或是一塊夠硬的石頭.
ETC_FA1_Line06.cn: 要把金属敲成形, 你需要一把锤子, 或是一块够硬的石头.

ETC_FA1_Line07.en: Yeah, it’s crude, but it works. Bend it over something solid, like a cinder block.
ETC_FA1_Line07.ch: 沒錯, 手法是很粗糙, 但管用. 找個硬東西把它折彎, 像水泥磚就行.
ETC_FA1_Line07.cn: 没错, 手法是很粗糙, 但管用. 找个硬东西把它折弯, 像水泥砖就行.

ETC_FA1_Line08.en: Remember, sharp edges can cut deep, so wear gloves or wrap your hands in cloth if that's all you've got.
ETC_FA1_Line08.ch: 記住, 金屬的銳邊割得很深, 所以一定要戴手套. 手邊只有布的話, 就拿布把手包起來.
ETC_FA1_Line08.cn: 记住, 金属的锐边割得很深, 所以一定要戴手套. 手边只有布的话, 就拿布把手包起来.

ETC_FA1_Line09.en: Metal is your friend out there.
ETC_FA1_Line09.ch: 在外頭, 金屬是你的好夥伴.
ETC_FA1_Line09.cn: 在外头, 金属是你的好伙伴.

ETC_FA1_Line10.en: Strong, durable, and it doesn't rot.
ETC_FA1_Line10.ch: 堅固, 耐用, 而且不會腐爛.
ETC_FA1_Line10.cn: 坚固, 耐用, 而且不会腐烂.

ETC_FA1_Line11.en: Stick with me, and you'll turn junk into defences that last.
ETC_FA1_Line11.ch: 跟著我學, 你就能把廢鐵變成撐得住的防禦工事.
ETC_FA1_Line11.cn: 跟着我学, 你就能把废铁变成撑得住的防御工事.

ETC_FA1_Line12.en: Stay safe, folks. Remember, survival isn't pretty, but it works.
ETC_FA1_Line12.ch: 各位, 注意安全. 記住, 求生不好看, 但活得下去.
ETC_FA1_Line12.cn: 各位, 注意安全. 记住, 求生不好看, 但活得下去.

ETC_FA1_Line13.en: I'll see you next time on 'Metal Matters.'
ETC_FA1_Line13.ch: 我們《金屬大小事》下次見.
ETC_FA1_Line13.cn: 我们《金属大小事》下次见.

ETC_FA2_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sharp hiss of a welding torch fills the air.** [img=music]
ETC_FA2_Line01.ch: [img=music] **空氣中充滿焊槍尖銳的嘶嘶聲.** [img=music]
ETC_FA2_Line01.cn: [img=music] **空气中充满焊枪尖锐的嘶嘶声.** [img=music]

ETC_FA2_Line02.en: Hey folks, I'm Dave, and this is 'Forge Ahead.'
ETC_FA2_Line02.ch: 嘿, 各位, 我是戴夫, 這裡是《鍛造前行》.
ETC_FA2_Line02.cn: 嘿, 各位, 我是戴夫, 这里是《锻造前行》.

ETC_FA2_Line03.en: Let's learn to weld like your life depends on it because it does.
ETC_FA2_Line03.ch: 焊接這門功夫, 要當成小命全靠它一樣認真學, 因為事實本來就是這樣.
ETC_FA2_Line03.cn: 焊接这门功夫, 要当成小命全靠它一样认真学, 因为事实本来就是这样.

ETC_FA2_Line04.en: First tip: safety. No goggles? Use a tinted visor or sunglasses.
ETC_FA2_Line04.ch: 第一個要訣: 安全. 沒有護目鏡? 拿有色面罩或太陽眼鏡頂著.
ETC_FA2_Line04.cn: 第一个要诀: 安全. 没有护目镜? 拿有色面罩或墨镜顶着.

ETC_FA2_Line05.en: Protect your eyes at all costs.
ETC_FA2_Line05.ch: 無論如何都要保護好眼睛.
ETC_FA2_Line05.cn: 无论如何都要保护好眼睛.

ETC_FA2_Line06.en: Welding rods? Grab some from old tools or scrap metal.
ETC_FA2_Line06.ch: 焊條呢? 從舊工具或廢金屬上弄一些就有了.
ETC_FA2_Line06.cn: 焊条呢? 从旧工具或废金属上弄一些就有了.

ETC_FA2_Line07.en: Start with small projects, like patching holes in a door or fence.
ETC_FA2_Line07.ch: 先從小東西練起, 像是補門板或圍欄上的破洞.
ETC_FA2_Line07.cn: 先从小东西练起, 像是补门板或围栏上的破洞.

ETC_FA2_Line08.en: Keep your hands steady and take your time.

ETC_FA2_Line09.en: A good weld can mean the difference between safety and a breach.
ETC_FA2_Line09.ch: 焊得好不好, 差別就在守得住還是被攻破.
ETC_FA2_Line09.cn: 焊得好不好, 差别就在守得住还是被攻破.

ETC_FA2_Line10.en: Stay safe out there, and keep building.
ETC_FA2_Line10.ch: 在外頭注意安全, 繼續動手做.
ETC_FA2_Line10.cn: 在外头注意安全, 继续动手做.

ETC_FA2_Line11.en: This is Dave, signing off from 'Forge Ahead.'
ETC_FA2_Line11.ch: 我是戴夫, 《鍛造前行》下次再會.
ETC_FA2_Line11.cn: 我是戴夫, 《锻造前行》下次再会.

ETC_FA3_Line01.en: [img=music] **The sharp sizzle of a welding torch igniting is heard.** [img=music]
ETC_FA3_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來焊槍點燃時尖銳的嘶嘶聲.** [img=music]
ETC_FA3_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来焊枪点燃时尖锐的嘶嘶声.** [img=music]

ETC_FA3_Line02.en: Hello, I'm Dave, and this is 'Forge Ahead.'
ETC_FA3_Line02.ch: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 這裡是《鍛造前行》.
ETC_FA3_Line02.cn: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 这里是《锻造前行》.

ETC_FA3_Line03.en: Today, we'll focus on repairing metal fences to secure your perimeter.
ETC_FA3_Line03.ch: 今天我們要專講金屬圍欄的修補, 把你的外圍守好.
ETC_FA3_Line03.cn: 今天我们要专讲金属围栏的修补, 把你的外围守好.

ETC_FA3_Line04.en: Inspect the fence for rust or damage.
ETC_FA3_Line04.ch: 先檢查圍欄有沒有生鏽或破損.
ETC_FA3_Line04.cn: 先检查围栏有没有生锈或破损.

ETC_FA3_Line05.en: Clean the area thoroughly before welding to ensure a strong bond.
ETC_FA3_Line05.ch: 焊之前把要接的部位徹底清乾淨, 接合才會夠牢.
ETC_FA3_Line05.cn: 焊之前把要接的部位彻底清干净, 接合才会够牢.

ETC_FA3_Line06.en: Use available materials like metal scraps to reinforce weak spots.
ETC_FA3_Line06.ch: 手邊有什麼就用什麼, 像廢金屬就能拿來補強脆弱的地方.
ETC_FA3_Line06.cn: 手边有什么就用什么, 像废金属就能拿来加固脆弱的地方.

ETC_FA3_Line07.en: A well-maintained fence can deter unwanted intrusions.
ETC_FA3_Line07.ch: 保養得好的圍欄, 能擋掉不速之客.
ETC_FA3_Line07.cn: 保养得好的围栏, 能挡掉不速之客.

ETC_FA3_Line08.en: Safety is paramount. Always protect your eyes and hands when working with metal.
ETC_FA3_Line08.ch: 安全第一. 處理金屬時, 永遠要保護好你的眼睛和雙手.
ETC_FA3_Line08.cn: 安全第一. 处理金属时, 永远要保护好你的眼睛和双手.

ETC_FA3_Line09.en: Stay vigilant, and keep forging ahead.
ETC_FA3_Line09.ch: 保持警覺, 繼續鍛造前行.
ETC_FA3_Line09.cn: 保持警惕, 继续锻造前行.

ETC_FA4_Line01.en: [img=music] **The gentle whoosh of a torch melting glass is heard.** [img=music]
ETC_FA4_Line01.ch: [img=music] **傳來噴槍熔化玻璃時輕柔的呼呼聲.** [img=music]
ETC_FA4_Line01.cn: [img=music] **传来喷枪熔化玻璃时轻柔的呼呼声.** [img=music]

ETC_FA4_Line02.en: Welcome to 'Forge Ahead.' I'm Alice, here to explore glassworking!
ETC_FA4_Line02.ch: 歡迎收看《鍛造前行》. 我是愛麗絲, 今天要帶大家認識玻璃工藝!
ETC_FA4_Line02.cn: 欢迎收看《锻造前行》. 我是爱丽丝, 今天要带大家认识玻璃工艺!

ETC_FA4_Line03.en: Broken windows can be a security risk.
ETC_FA4_Line03.ch: 破掉的窗戶是個安全漏洞.
ETC_FA4_Line03.cn: 损坏的窗户是个安全漏洞.

ETC_FA4_Line04.en: Salvage glass panes from abandoned buildings to replace damaged ones.
ETC_FA4_Line04.ch: 去廢棄建築裡拆玻璃, 拿來替換破掉的那幾片.
ETC_FA4_Line04.cn: 去废弃建筑里拆玻璃, 拿来替换损坏的那几片.

ETC_FA4_Line05.en: To cut glass, score it with a glass cutter or a sharp tool, then snap it along the line.
ETC_FA4_Line05.ch: 要裁玻璃, 先用玻璃刀或尖銳工具劃出刻痕, 再沿著線把它折斷.
ETC_FA4_Line05.cn: 要裁玻璃, 先用玻璃刀或尖锐工具划出刻痕, 再沿着线把它折断.

ETC_FA4_Line06.en: Always wear gloves to protect your hands.
ETC_FA4_Line06.ch: 記得全程戴手套保護雙手.
ETC_FA4_Line06.cn: 记得全程戴手套保护双手.

ETC_FA4_Line07.en: In emergencies, melted glass can be fashioned into simple containers or lenses.
ETC_FA4_Line07.ch: 緊急的時候, 熔化的玻璃還能做成簡單的容器或鏡片.
ETC_FA4_Line07.cn: 紧急的时候, 熔化的玻璃还能做成简单的容器或镜片.

ETC_FA4_Line08.en: Heat it until pliable, then shape as needed.
ETC_FA4_Line08.ch: 加熱到可以塑形, 再照你要的樣子捏出來.
ETC_FA4_Line08.cn: 加热到可以塑形, 再照你要的样子捏出来.

ETC_FA4_Line09.ch: 玻璃工藝需要耐心, 也需要小心.
ETC_FA4_Line09.cn: 玻璃工艺需要耐心, 也需要小心.

ETC_FA4_Line10.en: Practice these techniques to maintain your shelter and tools.
ETC_FA4_Line10.ch: 多練這幾招, 就能把你的住處和工具維護好.
ETC_FA4_Line10.cn: 多练这几招, 就能把你的住处和工具维护好.

ETC_FA4_Line11.en: Stay safe, and join me next time on 'Forge Ahead.'
ETC_FA4_Line11.ch: 注意安全, 下次《鍛造前行》再見.
ETC_FA4_Line11.cn: 注意安全, 下次《锻造前行》再见.

ETC_FA5_Line01.en: [img=music] **The rhythmic sound of trowel against brick is faintly audible.** [img=music]
ETC_FA5_Line01.ch: [img=music] **隱約可以聽見抹刀敲在磚上的規律聲響.** [img=music]
ETC_FA5_Line01.cn: [img=music] **隐约可以听见抹刀敲在砖上的规律声响.** [img=music]

ETC_FA5_Line02.en: Hello, I'm Dave, and this is 'Forge Ahead.'
ETC_FA5_Line02.ch: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 這裡是《鍛造前行》.
ETC_FA5_Line02.cn: 大家好, 我是戴夫, 这里是《锻造前行》.

ETC_FA5_Line03.en: Today, we'll discuss masonry building structures that stand the test of time.
ETC_FA5_Line03.ch: 今天我們要聊石工, 蓋出經得起時間考驗的結構.
ETC_FA5_Line03.cn: 今天我们要聊石工, 盖出经得起时间考验的结构.

ETC_FA5_Line04.en: Bricks and mortar are the basics.
ETC_FA5_Line04.ch: 磚塊和砂漿是最基本的東西.
ETC_FA5_Line04.cn: 砖块和砂浆是最基本的东西.

ETC_FA5_Line05.en: Mix sand, lime, and water to create mortar.
ETC_FA5_Line05.ch: 把砂, 石灰和水混在一起, 就成了砂漿.
ETC_FA5_Line05.cn: 把砂, 石灰和水混在一起, 就成了砂浆.

ETC_FA5_Line06.en: Layer bricks with mortar to construct walls or repair existing ones.
ETC_FA5_Line06.ch: 用砂漿把磚一層層砌起來, 就能蓋新牆或修補舊牆.
ETC_FA5_Line06.cn: 用砂浆把砖一层层砌起来, 就能盖新墙或修补旧墙.

ETC_FA5_Line07.ch: 每一層都要確認是水平的.
ETC_FA5_Line07.cn: 每一层都要确认是水平的.

ETC_FA5_Line08.en: Use a plumb line or a makeshift equivalent to keep your structure straight and stable.
ETC_FA5_Line08.ch: 用鉛垂線, 或隨手做個替代品, 讓結構保持筆直穩固.
ETC_FA5_Line08.cn: 用铅垂线, 或随手做个替代品, 让结构保持笔直稳固.

ETC_FA5_Line09.en: Masonry adds durability to your defences.
ETC_FA5_Line09.ch: 石工能讓你的防禦更耐久.
ETC_FA5_Line09.cn: 石工能让你的防御更耐久.

ETC_FA5_Line10.en: A well-built wall can provide safety against both the elements and unwanted guests.
ETC_FA5_Line10.ch: 一道砌得好的牆, 既能擋風雨, 也能擋不速之客.
ETC_FA5_Line10.cn: 一道砌得好的墙, 既能挡风雨, 也能挡不速之客.

ETC_FA5_Line12.en: I'll see you next time on 'Forge Ahead.'

ETC_FT1_Line01.en: [img=music] **The distant sound of gunfire echoes softly.** [img=music]

ETC_FT1_Line03.en: I'm Sergeant Davis, here to enhance your aiming skills.
ETC_FT1_Line03.ch: 我是戴維斯中士, 這堂課要提升各位的瞄準能力.
ETC_FT1_Line03.cn: 我是戴维斯中士, 这堂课要提升各位的瞄准能力.

ETC_FT1_Line04.en: Proper aiming increases your accuracy, ensuring each shot counts.
ETC_FT1_Line04.ch: 瞄準確實, 命中率就會提高, 每一發都不浪費.
ETC_FT1_Line04.cn: 瞄准确实, 命中率就会提高, 每一发都不浪费.

ETC_FT1_Line05.en: Always align your sights with the target, and maintain a steady stance to reduce recoil.
ETC_FT1_Line05.ch: 準星務必對正目標, 站姿要穩, 才能減少後坐力.
ETC_FT1_Line05.cn: 准星务必对正目标, 站姿要稳, 才能减少后坐力.

ETC_FT1_Line06.en: One effective stance is the Weaver stance.
ETC_FT1_Line06.ch: 其中一種有效的姿勢叫韋弗式站姿.
ETC_FT1_Line06.cn: 其中一种有效的姿势叫韦弗式站姿.

ETC_FT1_Line07.en: This provides greater stability and accuracy.
ETC_FT1_Line07.ch: 它能提供更好的穩定性和精準度.
ETC_FT1_Line07.cn: 它能提供更好的稳定性和精准度.

ETC_FT1_Line08.en: Making it useful for shooting at multiple targets or when firing from behind cover.
ETC_FT1_Line08.ch: 對付多個目標, 或是從掩體後射擊時特別好用.
ETC_FT1_Line08.cn: 对付多个目标, 或是从掩体后射击时特别好用.

ETC_FT1_Line10.en: The more you train, the more your accuracy, precision, and range improve.
ETC_FT1_Line10.ch: 練得愈多, 命中率、精準度和射程都會跟著提升.
ETC_FT1_Line10.cn: 练得越多, 命中率、精准度和射程都会跟着提升.

ETC_FT1_Line11.en: Remember, firearms are tools of survival.
ETC_FT1_Line11.ch: 記住, 槍械是求生的工具.
ETC_FT1_Line11.cn: 记住, 枪械是求生的工具.

ETC_FT1_Line12.ch: 明智使用, 負起責任.
ETC_FT1_Line12.cn: 明智使用, 负起责任.

ETC_FT1_Line13.en: Stay sharp, and join me next time on 'Firearms Training.'
ETC_FT1_Line13.ch: 保持警覺, 我們《槍械訓練》下次見.
ETC_FT1_Line13.cn: 保持警惕, 我们《枪械训练》下次见.
